title: A Thumbs-Up, a Nod, a Bowl of Soup: The Fun Side of Getting Culture Wrong
title_zh: 一个竖大拇指、一次点头、一碗汤：把文化弄错时的乐趣
intro_zh: 本文约538词，围绕“跨文化交流的乐趣”展开，用厨房、课堂、小组作业等生活化场景说明：文化误解不只是障碍，也常常是笑声与友谊的开头。全文含6个CET-4核心词，句子难度中等，理解目标约85%-90%。

paragraphs.en: Last winter, in a crowded student kitchen in Manchester, Lin from Shanghai watched her Italian roommate drop red chili sauce into the tomato soup. 'Just a little,' Marco said, making a small pinch with his fingers. Lin nodded and smiled. Ten minutes later she took one spoonful and reached for a full glass of water. Both of them laughed for a long time. That small gesture became the first joke of their year together.
paragraphs.zh: 去年冬天，在曼彻斯特一间拥挤的学生厨房里，来自上海的林看着她的意大利室友往番茄汤里倒红辣椒酱。“就一点点，”马可说，用手指比了一个小小的捏取动作。林点点头，笑了笑。十分钟后，她舀了一勺，然后伸手去拿一整杯水。两个人大笑了很久。那个小小的手势，成了他们共同一年里的第一个笑话。

paragraphs.en: Such moments are the everyday entertainment of cross-cultural life. A 2021 survey of more than 2,000 exchange students in Europe found that 78 percent could remember a funny encounter within their first month abroad, and 61 percent said those moments helped them make their closest local friends. Misunderstandings, it seems, are not only obstacles. They are doors that open when someone is brave enough to laugh at herself.
paragraphs.zh: 这样的时刻正是跨文化生活里日常的乐趣来源。一项2021年针对欧洲两千多名交换生的调查发现，78%的人能记得出国第一个月里一次好笑的相遇，61%的人表示，正是那些时刻帮他们交到了最亲近的当地朋友。看来，误解不只是障碍，它们也是一扇扇门——只要有人敢于自嘲，门就会打开。

paragraphs.en: Body language is a rich source of surprise. In most of Europe a thumbs-up means 'good job', but in parts of the Middle East it is an insult. A nod of the head signals agreement in Beijing and Berlin, yet in Bulgaria it can mean the opposite. When Lin's Turkish classmate shook his head to say 'yes, please', she poured him no tea at all. The awkward silence lasted three seconds, and then the whole table was laughing.
paragraphs.zh: 肢体语言是“惊喜”的富矿。在欧洲大部分地区，竖起大拇指表示“干得好”，但在中东一些地方却是侮辱。点头在北京和柏林都表示同意，可在保加利亚，它可能表示相反的意思。当林的土耳其同学摇头表示“好的，请来一点”时，她一滴茶也没给他倒。尴尬的沉默持续了三秒，然后整桌人都笑了。

paragraphs.en: Words play similar tricks. In many Asian settings, a polite 'yes' may mean 'I hear you', not 'I agree'. British speakers often use 'interesting' to mean 'I am not sure about that'. A visitor who takes every word literally is soon confused, and sometimes slightly hurt. Curiosity is the better tool: asking 'What does that mean here?' costs nothing and usually earns a warm explanation.
paragraphs.zh: 词语也会玩类似的把戏。在许多亚洲场合，礼貌的“是”可能只表示“我听到了”，而不是“我同意”。英国人常用“interesting”表示“我不太确定”。一个把每句话都照字面理解的访客，很快就会困惑，有时还会有点受伤。好奇心是更好的工具：问一句“在这里那是什么意思？”不花什么代价，通常还能换来一番热情的解释。

paragraphs.en: The pleasure is not one-sided. Most people love explaining their own customs to a friendly outsider. When Lin asked why her German flatmate always knocked on the table instead of clapping after a seminar, the answer turned into a twenty-minute talk about university traditions. She learned something; he enjoyed the attention; the kitchen grew louder and warmer.
paragraphs.zh: 这种乐趣并不是单方面的。大多数人都乐于向友善的外来者解释自己的习俗。当林问她的德国室友，为什么研讨课结束后总是敲桌子而不是鼓掌时，这个答案变成了一场二十分钟的大学传统漫谈。她学到了东西，他享受了被关注的感觉，厨房也变得更热闹、更温暖。

paragraphs.en: Not every difference is funny at first. Silence, directness, or a firm handshake can feel cold to someone raised differently. The trick is to adapt slowly and to check your assumptions. When a project group of five nationalities first met in Lin's course, they spent two meetings arguing about deadlines before realizing that 'soon' meant Friday to one member and next month to another. Writing actual dates on the board solved it in five minutes.
paragraphs.zh: 并非每一种差异起初都好笑。沉默、直率，或者有力的握手，对在不同环境里长大的人来说，都可能显得冷淡。办法是慢慢适应，并且时时检查自己的想当然。当林的课程里由五个国籍组成的小组第一次碰面时，他们花了两次会的时间争论截止日期，后来才明白“很快”对一个成员意味着周五，对另一个却意味着下个月。把具体日期写在黑板上，五分钟就解决了问题。

paragraphs.en: Researchers have long noticed that people who live abroad tend to score higher on tests of flexible thinking. One explanation is simple practice: every day abroad, you must read situations with no script, guess, and then correct yourself. That habit makes surprises less frightening and more interesting. A student who can survive a confusing dinner party can usually survive a confusing meeting, too.
paragraphs.zh: 研究者早就注意到，在国外生活过的人在思维灵活性测试中往往得分更高。一种解释是简单的练习：在国外的每一天，你都得在没有剧本的情况下读懂处境，先猜一猜，再修正自己。这种习惯让意外不那么可怕，反而更有意思。一个能应付一顿让人摸不着头脑的晚餐的学生，通常也能应付一场让人摸不着头脑的会议。

paragraphs.en: The joy of crossing cultures is not that everyone becomes the same. It is the small shock, the laugh, the story you tell afterwards. Lin still cannot eat chili the way Marco does, but she now cooks tomato soup for friends and always warns them first. Keep asking, keep tasting, keep laughing, and the world gets a little larger with every meal.
paragraphs.zh: 跨文化的乐趣，并不在于所有人都变得一样，而在于那一点小小的惊讶、那一阵笑，以及事后你会讲给别人听的故事。林至今没法像马可那样吃辣，但她现在会给朋友做番茄汤，而且总先提醒一句。继续问，继续尝，继续笑，世界就会随着每一顿饭变得更大一点。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the passage?
options: Exchange students should avoid talking about food.
Cultural misunderstandings can be a source of laughter and friendship.
Body language is more important than spoken language.
Living abroad always makes people feel lonely.
questions.explain: 全文以厨房、餐桌、小组作业中的误解为例，反复强调误解不只是障碍，还能带来笑声与友谊，故答案为第二项。第一项与原文相反；第三项过度比较；第四项文中未提。

questions.q: What happened when Lin's Turkish classmate shook his head at the table?
options: He refused the tea because he disliked it.
He was angry about Marco's chili sauce.
Lin mistook his gesture and gave him no tea.
Lin asked him to explain the custom at once.
questions.explain: 原文说该同学摇头表示“好的，请来一点”，而林误解了这个动作，一滴茶都没倒，故为第三项。文中没有说明他讨厌茶或生气，也未提到林立刻追问原因。

questions.q: Why did the five-nation project group argue about deadlines?
options: They used the same word with very different meanings.
No one in the group owned a calendar.
They could not agree on who should lead the group.
Their teacher gave them the wrong information.
questions.explain: 争论源于“soon（很快）”一词在不同成员心里对应不同时间长度，属于词义理解差异，故为第一项。写日期解决问题，说明并非缺少日历；组长与教师信息文中均未提及。

questions.q: In the sentence 'A visitor who takes every word literally is soon confused', 'literally' most probably means ______.
options: after thinking for a long time
questions.explain: 该句与上文“礼貌的是可能只表示我听到了”相对，指按字面意思理解每个词的人容易困惑，故 literally 意为“按字面地”，选第二项。其余选项与词义无关。
